title: Rooms Keys Read — payload
description: What a member asks of their own key holder: one record of a room (`key`), or up to 32 (`keys`), read from the named host, checked and opened. Exactly one of `key` and `keys` is present. The outer document members (id, type, issuer, recipient, issuedAt, expiresAt, proof) are owned by the framework — SPEC §6.3.

roomId.description: The room to read from. The recipient MUST already hold group state for it.

host.description: The host to read from, as a DID. Named by the caller because nothing maps a room to its host — a room is portable, so a remembered host goes stale silently, and a room may be registered with more than one. A caller who names the wrong host learns so as a refusal from a party that does not serve this room, which is loud and immediate.

key.description: The record to read, alone. Exactly one of `key` and `keys` is present.

keys.description: Several records to read in one request, at most 32, each answered on its own in `results`, in this order. Exactly one of `key` and `keys` is present.

purpose.description: OPTIONAL. The one purpose the caller will use the content this request discloses for (VTI-ACL-103), as `RecordPurpose` defines it. A purpose not granted is refused with `purposeNotGranted`. May be omitted where exactly one purpose is granted, or `any`.

Response.description: Success response to rooms/keys/read. Type https://trusttasks.org/spec/rooms/keys/read/0.2#response. For a request naming `key`, the record and its verdict, as in 0.1, with `createdAt` and `createdBy`. For a request naming `keys`, `results`: one entry per key, each its own success or error.

version.description: The record's version at the host.

status.description: Curation state, passed through. A `retracted` record has no body: the tombstone is the answer, not a failure.

createdAt.description: When the host stored the record's first version, passed through from `rooms/records/get/0.3` exactly as served (`RecordMetadataV3.createdAt`). Absent where the host served none.

createdBy.description: The author of the record's first version as the host recorded it, passed through from `rooms/records/get/0.3` exactly as served — `open` and `attributed` rooms only (`RecordMetadataV3.createdBy`). Absent where the host served none.

bodyStoredAt.description: When the host stored the body this version carries, passed through from `rooms/records/get/0.3` exactly as served (`RecordMetadataV3.bodyStoredAt`). The recipient verifies the author's proof against the DID document as it stood then. Absent where the host served none.

author.description: The member who wrote it, where the tier discloses one. Absent on `private`, where authorship is inside the body the recipient just opened.

plaintext.description: The opened record, base64url — the sealed tiers. **Never the key**, which is the whole reason this task exists rather than the record being handed to the member to open. Spelled as `rooms/keys/open` spells it, because it is the same bytes by the same route.

cleartext.description: The record body on an `open` room, where there is nothing to open. Carried as itself rather than base64url so that the shape says which tier the member is on — a member ought to be able to tell that this room's host can read what they just read.

verification.description: What the recipient checked and what it found. REQUIRED: an agent that returns a record without saying what it checked has made the member's decision for them.

results.description: Present, and only present, when the request named `keys`: one entry per key, in the request's order. Each entry is that key's own answer — a record or an error — and one key's failure never fails another's.

Response.title: Rooms Keys Read — response payload

ReadResult.title: ReadResult

KeyError.title: KeyError
KeyError.description: Why one key of a batch read was not answered with a record: the code, and `details`, the key would have been refused with had it been read alone, carried in the shape a `trust-task-error` payload carries them.

code.description: A declared code of this specification, such as `rooms/keys/read:hostRefused`, `rooms/keys/read:cannotOpen` or `rooms/keys/read:notAttempted`, or a standard code (SPEC §8.3).

message.description: Human-readable. Not normative: a consumer acts on `code` and `details`, never on this.
